data.title: Discovering a JDK Race Condition, and Debugging It in 30 Minutes with Fray
data.author: aoli-al
data.article_summary:
文章描述了在使用Fray工具对Fray进行集成测试时，意外发现JDK中的一个死锁问题。问题出现在`ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor`中，当一个任务被调度而另一个线程同时执行关闭操作时，可能导致任务被无限期阻塞。

具体来说，当`ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor`处于`SHUTDOWN`状态时，`FutureTask.get`方法可能会无限期等待任务完成。问题源于`schedule`方法在检查执行状态时，假设如果处于`SHUTDOWN`状态，任务会被终止，但实际上任务可能未被处理也未被终止，导致死锁。

Fray通过其确定性回放和调度可视化功能，帮助开发者快速定位问题。在`schedule`和`shutdown`方法的交错执行中，任务未被正确添加到工作线程，且执行状态被错误地设置为`TERMINATED`，导致任务永远不会被执行。

这个问题揭示了JDK中一个潜在的竞态条件，虽然设计上有一些保护机制，但在特定时序下仍可能出现问题。

不同观点：
• [anorwell] 提到了在生产环境中遇到的ThreadPoolExecutor在关闭时挂起的问题，怀疑是JDK17的潜在问题。虽然问题很难在本地复现，但怀疑与讨论中的问题相关。此外，anorwell还提到了考虑使用Fray工具来测试并发问题，以捕捉分布式系统中的并发问题。
   
• [exabrial] 详细介绍了Fray工具的功能和优点，强调它可以帮助发现和调试复杂的竞态条件和死锁问题。同时，exabrial表达了对该工具在20年前尚未存在的遗憾，暗示该工具在当前具有很高的实用价值。

• [MaxBarraclough] 关注于通过人工引入sleep调用来重现死锁的问题，并提到修复该问题的进展。他还对修复该问题所需的代码行数表示好奇，提供了相关的GitHub链接和OpenJDK的bug追踪链接。

• [latchkey] 提出了一个与讨论主题无关的问题，表示代码中的文字难以阅读，因为字体颜色接近白色。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Fray工具在实际应用中的效果和适用范围，特别是在并行测试和fibers环境下的表现。

Bug Behavior
The
ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor
schedules tasks by adding them to a work queue and executing them in worker threads. Depending on the executor’s state, users would expect the following behavior:
State
ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.schedule
FutureTask.get
RUNNING
returns task
blocks until task completes
SHUTDOWN
throws
RejectedExecutionException
throws
CancellationException
However, Fray revealed that when the
ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor
is in the
SHUTDOWN
state, the
FutureTask.get
method may block indefinitely waiting for the task to complete.
How the Bug Occurs
The bug manifests when Fray interleaves the
schedule
method and the
shutdown
method. At line 9 of
ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.schedule
, the executor tries to add a new worker to execute tasks. It first checks whether the executor is in a state that allows the task to run. If the executor is in the
SHUTDOWN
state, the
schedule
method assumes that the shutdown process will terminate the task, so it simply returns (Line 14) without creating a new worker thread. However, this assumption breaks when the shutdown method transitions to the
SHUTDOWN
state but will not terminate the task, leaving it in a limbo state.
The following stack traces illustrate the problematic interleaving. The main thread (test worker) is going to create a new worker for the task, while the shutdown thread (Thread-3) is executing
tryTerminate
and setting the state to
TIDYING
.
Next, Fray yields to the main thread, which performs the condition check at line 10 of
ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.schedule
. The executor is now in the
TIDYING
state, making both
runStateAtLeast(c, SHUTDOWN)
and
runStateAtLeast(c, STOP)
return true. The
schedule
method then returns the task without adding to a worker.
Meanwhile, in the shutdown thread, execution reaches
ctl.compareAndSet(c, ctlOf(TERMINATED, 0))
at line 16 of
ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.shutdown
. The
ctl
is set to
TERMINATED
, and the shutdown thread completes. At this point, no thread will execute or interrupt the task, leaving it blocked forever.
More Details
While the bug is conceptually simple, reaching this state is not straightforward because
ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor
and
ThreadPoolExecutor
are designed to prevent such situations. For example, in the
tryTerminate
method (Line 23-29),
ThreadPoolExecutor
checks whether the work queue is empty and workers are interrupted before setting the state to
TIDYING
. However, Fray demonstrates that this check can be bypassed if execution of
super.getQueue().add(task)

data.title: Joining Apple Computer (2018)
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Bill Atkinson回顾了他40年前加入苹果公司的经历。1978年，正在华盛顿大学攻读神经科学博士学位的他，受到老友Jef Raskin邀请加入苹果。尽管最初犹豫，但在Steve Jobs的劝说和启发下，他决定退学加入苹果。Jobs以“冲浪在浪潮前沿”的比喻打动了他，使他看到在苹果可以开创未来。Atkinson在苹果参与了多个重要项目，包括将UCSD Pascal系统移植到Apple II，并为Lisa项目引入了鼠标作为标准配置。他还开发了QuickDraw图形系统和Lisa窗口、事件、菜单管理器，并发明了下拉菜单。这些贡献为苹果的图形界面发展奠定了基础。Atkinson与Jobs密切合作，彼此激发创意，共同推动了苹果产品的创新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对苹果早期创始成员及其影响的回忆与反思，涉及个人成功因素、技术革新、现代科技对比以及对LSD影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• [r0m4n0] 认为技术天才和强大人脉关系可能共同促成了个人在顶级公司的成功。他提到了一些早期技术领袖之间的联系，并感慨拥有这些关系可能有助于解决财务问题。
• [duxup] 怀念科技行业的"旧时光"，那时一切皆有可能，技术环境更加开放和令人兴奋，而现在则感觉被广告和封闭的系统所限制。
• [kristianp] 提出问题，为什么一个神经科学博士生会被雇佣来写代码，并提供了一个采访链接以提供更多背景信息。
• [dedicate] 认为像HyperCard这样让非技术人员参与创造的工具代表了技术的进步，但当今的科技环境却似乎在倒退，出现了封闭的生态系统和应用商店。
• [acheron] 讨论了“亮色模式”的起源，并提到与LSD相关的创意决策背景，同时引发对技术决策背后的思考。

补充讨论：
• [JKCalhoun] 和 [swyx] 讨论了LSD对创意和创新的潜在影响，提到一些著名艺术家和创作者的例子，并思考这种影响是否是不可替代的。
• [tonyedgecombe] 批评John Sculley未能在苹果内部留住人才，认为他并不是带领苹果的合适人选。
• [gyomu] 强调苹果过去以赋能创意人群为使命，并认为这是吸引人们关注和 admiration 的原因，但今天这一使命是否仍然适用存在争议。
• 其他如[leyka], [FabHK], [Waterluvian], 和 [mrcwinn] 主要表达了对逝者的敬意和对其工作的感激之情。

争议焦点：
• 个人成功是否更多依赖于技术能力还是人脉关系。
• 现代科技是否在技术开放性和创新性上倒退。
• LSD等意识改变物质对创意和创新的实际影响及其伦理讨论。

Joining Apple Computer
Author:
Bill Atkinson
Date:
April 1979
Characters:
Bill Atkinson,     Jef Raskin,     Steve Jobs,     Susan Kare
Topics:
Inspiration,     MacPaint,     QuickDraw,     HyperCard
Summary:
Reflections on the 40th anniversary of my joining Apple
40 years ago today, I joined Apple Computer on April 27, 1978. It was a big turning point in my life and I am glad I said "Yes".
I was working on my PhD in neuroscience with Doug Bowden at the University of Washington Regional Primate Research Center. Jef Raskin, a professor and friend from my undergraduate days at UC San Diego, called and urged me to join him at an exciting new startup called Apple Computer.
I told him I had to finish my PhD, a required credential for researching brains and consciousness. But Jef would not take "No" for an answer, and sent me roundtrip airplane tickets with a note: "Just visit for a weekend, no strings attached." My dad lived in nearby Los Gatos so I decided to visit.
I don't know what Jef told Steve Jobs about me, but Steve spent the entire day recruiting me. He introduced me to all 30 employees at Apple Computer. They seemed intelligent and passionate, and looked like they were having fun, but that was not enough to lure me away from my graduate studies.
Toward the end of the day, Steve took me aside and told me that any hot new technology I read about was actually two years old. "There is a lag time between when someting is invented, and when it is available to the public. If you want to make a difference in the world, you have to be ahead of that lag time. Come to Apple where you can invent the future and change millions of people's lives."
Then he gave me a visual: "Think how fun it is to surf on the front edge of a wave, and how not-fun to dog paddle on the tail edge of the same wave." That image persuaded me, and within two weeks I had quit my graduate program, moved to Silicon Valley, and was working at Apple Computer. I never finished my neuroscience degree, and my dad was mad at me for wasting ten years of college education that he helped to pay for. I was pretty nervous, but knew I had made the right choice.
Steve Jobs and I became close friends. We went for long walks at Castle Rock State Park, shared meals and wide-ranging conversations about life and design. We bounced ideas off each other. Sometimes he would start a conversation with "Here's a crazy idea...", and the idea would go back and forth and evolve into a serious discussion, or occasionally a workable design. Steve listened to me and challenged me. His support at Apple allowed me to made a difference in the world.
I wanted to port the UCSD Pascal system to the Apple II. We needed to build software in a cumulative fashion with libraries of reusable modules, and Apple BASIC didn't even have local variables. My manager said "No", but I went over his head to Steve. Steve thought Apple users were fine with BASIC and 6502 assembly language, but since I argued so passionately, he would give me two weeks to prove him wrong. Within hours I boarded a plane to San Diego, worked like crazy for two weeks, and returned with a working UCSD Pascal System that Apple ended up using to bootstrap the Lisa development.
After the UCSD Pascal system shipped, Steve asked me to work on on Apple's new Lisa project. The Apple II had optional game paddle knobs, but software writers could not count on them because not every user had them. I convinced project manager Tom Whitney that the Lisa computer needed to include a mouse in the box so we could write software that counted on a pointing device. Otherwise a graphics editor would have to be designed to be usable with only cursor keys.
The Apple II displayed white text on a black background. I argued that to do graphics properly we had to switch to a white background like paper. It works fine to invert text when printing, but it would not work for a photo to be printed in negative. The Lisa hardware team complained the screen would flicker too much, and they would need faster refresh with more expensive RAM to prevent smearing when scrolling. Steve listened to all the pros and cons then sided with a white background for the sake of graphics.
The Lisa and Macintosh were designed with full bitmap displays. This gave tremendous flexibility in what you could draw, but at a big cost. There were a lot of pixels to set and clear anytime you wanted to draw a character, line, image, or area. I wrote the optimized assembly language QuickDraw graphics primitives that all Lisa and Macintosh applications called to write the pixels. QuickDraw performance made the bitmap display and graphical user interface practical
(see
I Still Remember Regions
)
.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[对一种新型轻轨系统的不同看法和讨论，包括其创新性、成本效益、技术选择以及与现有交通系统的对比]

不同观点：
• **支持创新和成本节约的观点**（habosa）：该评论介绍了这种“非常”轻便的轻轨系统的特点，如电池供电、无需架空电线、可在狭小空间内转弯等，认为该设计能大幅降低成本，并提供高频、便捷的服务。
• **对成本效益的质疑**（andrewl-hn）：该评论以法国贝桑松的常规有轨电车为例，指出其极具成本效益，并质疑这种新型轻轨是否能在成本上超越传统方案，尤其是在英国成本普遍较高的情况下。
• **历史对比和质疑**（PLenz）：该评论通过对比1896年的轻轨法案，指出这种“创新”实际上是对旧概念的重新包装，质疑其真正的创新性。
• **对车辆容量和设计的质疑**（rsynnott）：认为该轻轨车辆容量过小，甚至小于大多数公交车，质疑其能否有效服务于大量乘客。
• **对电池供电和轨道必要性的质疑**（ninalanyon）：质疑为何在使用电池供电的情况下仍需铺设轨道，而不是直接使用电动公交车。

补充讨论：
• **对“创新”的广泛批评**（bluGill）：该评论认为这种所谓的“创新”实际上并未解决任何实际问题，称之为“Gadgetbahn”（贬义词，指华而不实的交通项目）。指出创新应着重于解决系统性问题，而不是设计新奇但无实际效益的系统。同时提到购买标准化设备可以降低成本并保证长期维护。
• **英国与法国/欧盟的成本差异**（ClumsyPilot）：指出英国建设有轨电车的成本远高于法国/欧盟，主要因为英国的施工深度和保护公用设施的要求更高。
• **对项目实际应用的质疑**（JdeBP）：详细分析了考文垂的城市结构和历史背景，指出该城市的道路系统复杂且多为历史遗留，认为这种轻轨系统在实际应用中可能面临诸多限制，且可能更多是为了向其他城市推广。
• **对项目经济效益的质疑**（xnx）：认为任何基础设施项目都应在7年内看到投资回报，并提到自动驾驶技术（如Waymo）可能会对传统公共交通产生巨大冲击。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **对具体技术细节的关注**（tempodox）：指出车载显示屏在阳光下的可读性问题，建议使用更适合白天使用的显示屏。
• **个人经历和情感表达**（pkaodev）：不直接相关，但提到离开考文垂是其人生中最好的决定之一，对城市交通系统的评价较为负面。

争议焦点：
• 该轻轨系统是否真正具备创新性以及能否在成本上超越传统有轨电车方案。
• 电池供电和轨道设计的必要性以及车辆容量是否足够。
• 项目在考文垂实际应用的可行性和经济效益。

data.title: Field Notes from Shipping Real Code with Claude
data.author: diwank
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了通过AI助手Claude实现高效软件开发的实际方法。作者强调，实现10倍生产力提升并非靠魔法，而是通过一系列严谨的实践，放大AI的优势并弥补其不足。文章详细描述了在Julep使用的实际基础设施，包括CLAUDE.md模板、提交策略和防止灾难性发布的保障措施。最重要的是，作者指出，即使在AI时代，编写测试代码仍然是至关重要的。文章还探讨了AI辅助开发的三种模式，并强调良好的开发实践是AI放大能力而非混乱的关键。通过真实部署和深夜调试的经验，作者分享了实际有效的模式，而非理论或短期实验得出的结论。最终，文章揭示了“氛围编码”（vibe-coding）的深层含义，将其比作指挥乐队，而非单纯依赖AI生成代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI辅助开发中的实践与争议

不同观点：
• 作者（diwank）支持在代码库中使用特定的注释格式（如Anchor Comments），以方便知识的嵌入和检索，特别是对复杂或重要的代码部分进行标记。这种做法有助于系统化地管理代码并提高效率。
• kasey_junk认为AI推动了开发者对系统化验证过程的投资，这些过程虽然重要但以前常被忽视。AI的不确定性可以作为一种信号，促使开发者去建立更完善的验证系统。
• m_kos对AI工具（如Sonnet 4）的可靠性提出质疑，指出其在代码生成和报告中的错误，并提到其他用户似乎没有类似问题，质疑是否是自己使用的问题。
• nxobject指出文档和注释的实践不必特定于AI，可以适用于任何代码库，对不熟悉代码的贡献者同样有帮助。
• dkobia强调了在LLM辅助开发中保持目标导向的重要性，避免过度关注实现细节而偏离实际目标。
• wonger_质疑在代码库中组织LLM提示和注释的方式是否可以更优雅，并提出关于“vibe-coding”定义的讨论，同时关注代码发送至LLM前的处理问题。
• remram仅对文章顶部的图片加载速度提出技术性问题，未涉及核心讨论。
• skerit支持在复杂项目中使用更高级的AI模型（如Claude Opus），并质疑Anthropic对不同模型层的定价策略。
• mgraczyk反对作者不信任AI编写测试的观点，认为AI生成测试后的人工审查和调整是可行的做法。
• __mharrison__对其他工具和模型的使用经验表示好奇，未明确立场。
• lispisok支持让AI参与测试的初步编写，认为人类应承担最终责任，并质疑作者对测试和迁移的严格限制是出于对团队不信任。
• nilirl对模型特定注释造成的视觉噪音表示不满，并质疑这种做法是否比传统开发方式更高效。
• Artoooooor分享了个人使用Claude Code的体验，虽然高效但成本高昂，认为依赖AI是不可避免的趋势。
• meeech以幽默方式质疑文章本身由人类和机器编写的比例。

补充讨论：
• AI生成代码的可靠性和成本问题引发了不同用户的关注和讨论。
• 对AI在测试编写中的角色存在争议，部分用户认为人类应严格审查和调整AI生成的测试。
• 注释和文档的组织方式及其对代码可读性的影响也是讨论的焦点之一。
• 对不同AI模型（如Opus和Sonnet）的使用体验和定价策略存在不同看法。

争议焦点：
• AI在编写测试和数据迁移等关键任务中的可信度和人类责任问题。
• 注释和文档的组织方式是否高效及其对代码可读性的影响。
• AI工具（如Sonnet 4）的可靠性和用户体验问题。

June 7, 2025
Field Notes From Shipping Real Code With Claude
Vibe Coding Isn’t Just a Vibe
Shimmering Substance - Jackson Pollock
Think of this post as your field guide to a new way of building software. By the time you finish reading, you’ll understand not just the how but the why behind AI-assisted development that actually works.
Here’s What You’re Going to Learn
First, we’ll explore how to genuinely achieve that mythical 10x productivity boost—not through magic, but through deliberate practices that amplify AI’s strengths while compensating for its weaknesses. You’ll discover why some developers ship features in hours while others fight their AI tools for days.
Next, I’ll walk you through the exact infrastructure we use at Julep to ship production code daily with Claude’s help. This isn’t theoretical—it’s battle-tested on a codebase serving real users with real money on the line. You’ll see our
CLAUDE.md
templates, our commit strategies, and the guardrails that keep us from shipping disasters.
Most importantly, you’ll understand why writing your own tests remains absolutely sacred, even (especially) in the age of AI. This single principle will save you from the midnight debugging sessions that plague developers who hand over too much control to their AI assistants.
We’ll explore the three distinct modes of AI-assisted development, each with its own rhythms and rules. Like a musician learning when to play forte versus pianissimo, you’ll develop an intuition for when to let AI lead versus when to take firm control.
But here’s the real insight:
Good development practices aren’t just nice-to-haves anymore—they’re the difference between AI that amplifies your capabilities and AI that amplifies your chaos. The research bears this out dramatically.
1
Teams using rigorous practices deploy 46 times more frequently and are 440 times faster from commit to deployment. When you add AI to disciplined practices, these numbers don’t just add—they multiply.
Why This Post Exists: From Meme to Method
Let me take you back to when this all started.
2
Andrej Karpathy
3
tweeted about “vibe-coding”—this idea of letting AI write your code while you just vibe. The developer community had a good laugh. It sounded like the ultimate developer fantasy: kick back, sip coffee, let the machines do the work.
The birth of “vibe coding”
Then
Anthropic
released Sonnet 3.7 and Claude Code
, and something unexpected happened. The joke stopped being funny because it started being… possible? Of course, our trusty friend
Cursor
had been around awhile but this new interface finally felt like
true vibe coding
.
At
Julep
, we build complex AI workflow orchestration. Imagine trying to explain to an AI assistant a codebase that includes
FastAPI
services talking to
Temporal
workflows, all backed by a
TimescaleDB
database with
4
vector embeddings, documented in
TypeSpec
, and organized in a
5
monorepo that would make most developers weep. Our backend isn’t just complex—it’s a living, breathing system with years of accumulated decisions, patterns, and occasional technical debt.
We have taken the utmost care to keep code quality high, and ample documentation for ourselves. However, the sheer size, and historical context of
why
different parts of the code are organized the way they are takes weeks for a good engineer to grok. Getting AI to understand this interconnected maze felt like teaching calculus to someone who just learned arithmetic. But here’s what we discovered: Claude Code is intentionally low-level and unopinionated, providing close to raw model access without forcing specific workflows. This design philosophy creates something powerful—a tool that adapts to your workflow rather than forcing you into its box.
The flexibility, though, is a double-edged sword. Without proper guardrails, you’re not coding anymore—you’re playing whack-a-mole with an overeager intern who has memorized Stack Overflow but never shipped production code.
This post shares what actually works. Not the theory from blog posts written by people who tried AI coding for a weekend. These are patterns forged in the fire of actual deploys, 3 AM debugging sessions, and the unforgiving reality of users who expect their workflows to actually work.
Understanding Vibe-Coding: More Than Meets the Eye
‘pls fix’
6
Steve Yegge
brilliantly coined the term
CHOP
—Chat-Oriented Programming in a slightly-dramatic-titled post
“The death of the junior developer”
. It’s a perfect description of the surface mechanics: you chat with an AI until code materializes. But after months of living this workflow, I’ve come to understand it’s much deeper than that.
Think of traditional coding like sculpting marble. You start with a blank block and carefully chisel away, line by line, function by function. Every stroke is deliberate, every decision yours. It’s satisfying but slow.
Vibe-coding is more like conducting an orchestra. You’re not playing every instrument—you’re directing, shaping, guiding. The AI

• 注释和文档的组织方式是否高效及其对代码可读性的影响。
• AI工具（如Sonnet 4）的可靠性和用户体验问题。

data.title: Why Understanding Software Cycle Time Is Messy, Not Magic
data.author: SiempreViernes
data.article_summary: 文章《No Silver Bullets: Why Understanding Software Cycle Time is Messy, Not Magic》通过分析超过55,000个观察数据，研究影响软件开发周期时间的因素。作者使用贝叶斯层次模型，区分个体和组织差异，探讨编码时间、任务范围和协作模式对周期时间的影响。研究发现，尽管工作场所因素对周期时间有预期中的影响，但这些影响相对 modest（ modest：适度的），且存在显著的个体和组织间差异。文章强调，单个观察数据对典型性能的反映有限，提升软件交付速度需要系统层面的思考，而非仅关注个体干预。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"周期时间"（cycle time）作为开发过程中的衡量指标的讨论，包括其意义、使用方式、局限性以及与其他因素的关系。

不同观点：
• **tangotaylor**：认为周期时间的变化具有趣味性，比如六月和七月周期时间略微下降。同时，通过图表观察到，增加编码天数对周期时间的提升效果递减，而每个PR的评论越多，周期时间会明显变慢，其个人经验验证了这一点。

• **tmnvdb**：不认为周期时间应该用于评估个体开发者的生产力，强调周期时间应捕捉系统性的低效和瓶颈，而不是个人努力。Kanban方法论中，周期时间及其变异性常用于预测交付时间线。

• **SiempreViernes**：引用文章内容，指出周期时间与多种因素（如每周编码天数、合并PR数量、协作程度）之间存在精确但 modest 的关联，个体之间和内部仍有大量未解释的差异。

• **duncanfwalker**：质疑用每个PR的评论数量衡量协作深度，认为这可能与实际协作程度呈负相关，高水平团队的PR评论可能很少，而缺乏支持的初级开发者的PR评论则可能很多。

• **wry_durian**：指出周期时间的三个问题：它只是总成本方程的代理变量、滞后指标、以及队列大小对下游经济问题的影响更大，建议在考虑周期时间之前先考虑队列大小。

• **dgfitz**：指出其所在组织的周期时间可长达一年，嵌入式开发和有限的发布节奏使得Jira等工作流不适用，质疑研究是否仅针对web开发。

• **resource_waste**：分享个人经验，提到其时间估算总是错误，即使分解任务后仍然如此，常需将初始估算乘以3才能接近实际时间。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：周期时间是否适合作为衡量个体生产力的指标。tangotaylor和SiempreViernes关注周期时间的实际变化和关联，而tmnvdb和duncanfwalker则质疑其在个体层面的适用性。

• 其他讨论要点：wry_durian强调队列大小对经济问题的影响更大，建议从更广泛的角度看待开发流程中的问题。dgfitz指出不同开发环境（如嵌入式开发）中周期时间的不同表现。resource_waste分享了时间估算困难的个人经验，与周期时间的讨论有一定关联。

Title:
No Silver Bullets: Why Understanding Software Cycle Time is Messy, Not Magic
Authors:
John C. Flournoy
,
Carol S. Lee
,
Maggie Wu
,
Catherine M. Hicks
View a PDF of the paper titled No Silver Bullets: Why Understanding Software Cycle Time is Messy, Not Magic, by John C. Flournoy and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Understanding factors that influence software development velocity is crucial for engineering teams and organizations, yet empirical evidence at scale remains limited. A more robust understanding of the dynamics of cycle time may help practitioners avoid pitfalls in relying on velocity measures while evaluating software work. We analyze cycle time, a widely-used metric measuring time from ticket creation to completion, using a dataset of over 55,000 observations across 216 organizations. Through Bayesian hierarchical modeling that appropriately separates individual and organizational variation, we examine how coding time, task scoping, and collaboration patterns affect cycle time while characterizing its substantial variability across contexts. We find precise but modest associations between cycle time and factors including coding days per week, number of merged pull requests, and degree of collaboration. However, these effects are set against considerable unexplained variation both between and within individuals. Our findings suggest that while common workplace factors do influence cycle time in expected directions, any single observation provides limited signal about typical performance. This work demonstrates methods for analyzing complex operational metrics at scale while highlighting potential pitfalls in using such measurements to drive decision-making. We conclude that improving software delivery velocity likely requires systems-level thinking rather than individual-focused interventions.

data.title: FAA to eliminate floppy disks used in air traffic control systems
data.author: daledavies
data.article_summary: 美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）计划升级陈旧的空中交通管制（ATC）系统，以取代目前仍在使用软盘和纸条的过时技术。现行系统硬件老化，难以持续维护，存在重大安全隐患。FAA代理局长Chris Rocheleau表示，将全面替换旧系统，确保其更安全、防黑客攻击。然而，由于该系统需24/7运行，升级不能简单关闭替换，且需防范任何潜在网络攻击。白宫尚未公布升级成本，FAA已开始向企业征集方案，并计划举办“行业日”活动。尽管交通部希望四年内完成，但专家认为时间表不现实。升级刻不容缓，因现系统已多年未更新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于空中交通管制系统（ATC）仍在使用软盘等过时技术的讨论

不同观点：
• 一些人认为如果现有系统有效，就不应改变。例如，[evanjrowley]表示信任基于Windows 95和软盘的系统，质疑现代系统的可靠性，甚至对未来可能加入AI的设想表示怀疑。
• 另一部分人关注其他国家的做法，[ic_fly2]和[staplung]提到报告中未提及其他国家的ATC系统是否也使用软盘，或者是否已经进行了升级，并认为这些信息具有参考价值。
• 关于系统升级的技术方案，存在不同建议：
  - [branon]建议使用GNU/Linux运行DOSBox来保留软件栈，以此替代现有硬件和软件。
  - [burnt-resistor]和[asdefghyk]提到可以使用固态软盘仿真器，以减少机械故障的风险。
  - [ThinkBeat]提议将系统虚拟化，以便更容易维护旧计算机，并认为开发新系统需要很长时间。

补充讨论：
• 政治和经济因素也被提及，[latexr]质疑在当前政治气候和政府削减重要服务的情况下，是否是进行如此重要转型的合适时机。
• [heisenbit]强调了纸质备份的可靠性，认为在新的系统可能存在早期漏洞的情况下，独立的备份系统是必要的。
• [osigurdson]指出大软件咨询服务公司与政府机构合作时，往往优先考虑收入和降低自身风险，而非系统的现代化。
• [kgwxd]对信息来源的可信度提出质疑，认为提供信息的个人可能有动机破坏联邦政府以让位于私营企业。
• [jeffreygoesto]提到通过媒体了解到了这一情况，表明公众对该问题的关注。
• 最后，[ralphc]对选择Windows 95而非更健壮的NT系统表示不解。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于是否应替换现有的基于软盘的ATC系统，以及如何在保持系统稳定性和安全性的前提下进行升级。一方认为现有系统只要有效就不应改变，另一方则认为技术升级势在必行，并提出了多种技术解决方案。

44215197.article_content:
(Image credit: Shutterstock)
The head of the Federal Aviation Administration just outlined an ambitious goal to upgrade the U.S.’s air traffic control (ATC) system and bring it into the 21st century. According to
NPR
, most ATC towers and other facilities today feel like they’re stuck in the 20th century, with controllers using paper strips and floppy disks to transfer data, while their computers run Windows 95. While this likely saved them from the
disastrous CrowdStrike outage
that had a massive global impact, their age is a major risk to the nation’s critical infrastructure, with the FAA itself saying that the current state of its hardware is unsustainable.
“The whole idea is to replace the system. No more floppy disks or paper strips,” acting FAA administrator Chris Rocheleau told the House Appropriations Committee last Wednesday. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy also said earlier this week,” This is the most important infrastructure project that we’ve had in this country for decades. Everyone agrees — this is non-partisan. Everyone knows we have to do it.”
The aviation industry put up a coalition pushing for ATC modernization called
Modern Skies
, and it even ran an ad telling us that ATC is still using floppy disks and several older technologies to keep our skies safe.
You may like

Prominent Computex sign runs Windows 7, as Microsoft insists we move on from Windows 10
U.S. Gov't eliminates tape data storage at the GSA to save $1M per year, but tape isn't dead yet
Modern Skies - The Time for Change is NOW - YouTube
Watch On
Unfortunately, upgrading the ATC system isn’t as simple as popping into your nearby Micro Center and buying the latest and greatest gaming PC. First and foremost, some systems can never be shut down because it is crucial for safety. Because of this, you can’t just switch off one site to swap out ancient components for newer ones. Aside from that, the upgrades to this critical infrastructure should be resistant to hacking and other vulnerabilities, as even a single breach could cripple the nation, costing time, money, and lives.
The FAA is pouring a lot of money into maintaining its old ATC systems, as they have to keep running 24/7. Nevertheless, age will eventually catch up no matter how much repair, upkeep, or overhaul you do. Currently, the White House hasn’t said what this update will cost. The FAA has already put out a Request For Information to gather data from companies willing to take on the challenge of upgrading the entire system. It also announced several ‘Industry Days’ so companies can pitch their tech and ideas to the Transportation Department.
Duffy said that the Transportation Department aims to complete the project within four years. However, industry experts say this timeline is unrealistic. No matter how long it takes, it’s high time that the FAA upgrades the U.S.’s ATC system today after decades of neglect.

data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者从Emacs转向Obsidian的经历和原因。Emacs是一个强大但复杂的文本编辑器，具备如Org-Mode等工具，可以用于代码管理、任务跟踪和笔记管理等，但需要大量自定义和插件维护。作者最终因不想再花费精力处理这些复杂配置，转而使用更现代、简便的工具Obsidian。Obsidian是一款基于Markdown的笔记应用，拥有丰富的社区插件支持，且移动端体验更佳。作者计划采用PARA方法（项目、领域、资源、归档）在Obsidian中管理个人知识，以实现更简单和一致的工作流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在AI时代保持独立思考能力以及工具（如Emacs、Obsidian等）的选择与使用对思维和知识管理的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持通过特定工具和方法训练独立思考能力**：  
  - [thorum] 推荐 Henrik Karlsson 的博客，认为他的文章可以帮助训练思维，产生原创想法，并提高独立解决问题的能力。
  - [briian] 提出延迟使用AI解决问题的建议，认为这样可以训练大脑，同时提高AI系统的实用性，因为更好的提示词能提升AI的表现。

• **Emacs工具的优劣**：  
  - [8s2ngy] 认为Emacs功能强大但需要大量插件和自定义配置，最终因维护成本高而放弃，倾向于更现代、简化的工具。
  - [cjauvin] 也认为Emacs需要大量投入，但可以通过混合使用多种工具来解决不同问题，不必局限于单一工具。
  - [8s2ngy]（同一人）的补充观点：Emacs不需要大量插件，简单的配置也能长期有效，但承认需要投入时间阅读文档。

• **Obsidian与Emacs等工具的对比**：  
  - [agnishom] 对Obsidian持怀疑态度，认为其不开源且由小团队维护，存在公司倒闭的风险。
  - [zackify] 正在开发Revect工具，希望通过集成Obsidian与AI聊天记录，实现数据的持久化和自主拥有。
  - [minikomi] 认为结合GPT等AI工具自动拉取相关笔记是非常好的做法。

• **数字化与传统工具的比较**：  
  - [bob1029] 更喜欢用纸笔记录，认为数字工具容易分心，纸笔的物理限制反而能帮助更好地管理信息。
  - [leakycap] 则依赖Macintosh Finder这样熟悉的老系统来管理个人知识，认为工具的熟悉度对知识管理很重要。

• **AI在知识管理和笔记整理中的作用**：  
  - [jiri] 关心如何在AI时代有效地管理个人知识，包括是否应该存储聊天记录以及如何有效检索之前的信息。
  - [kreyenborgi] 使用Emacs中的gptel工具，结合AI和传统笔记管理，认为这种方法实用且有效。
  - [ebiester] 认为AI在组织笔记方面还不够成熟，主要问题在于笔记的上下文缺乏，搜索时不如预期有效。

• **对工具迷恋的批评**：  
  - [bsenftner] 批评一些开发者过度迷恋工具本身，认为工具应为目的服务，过度关注工具本身会混淆工具与知识的本质。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Emacs等工具的复杂性和维护成本与其功能强大之间的平衡，以及AI在知识管理和思维训练中的实际作用和局限性。
• **工具选择多样性**：许多评论者提到混合使用多种工具以适应不同需求，而不是依赖单一工具。
• **AI作为辅助工具的角色**：大多数评论者认为AI应作为辅助工具，而不是取代个人思考和知识管理的核心。

44214481.article_content:
The Joy (and pain) of Emacs
​
I use emacs, which might be thought of as a thermonuclear word processor.
—Neal Stephenson,
In the Beginning was the Command Line
Some years ago, I went through a phase that I imagine many software developers go through at least once in their careers—a period of intense fascination with
Emacs
. "Emacs is a great operating system that only lacks a decent text editor", as the old joke goes. This rang fairly true in my own experience. Emacs is ostensibly a text editor, but really it is a gateway to a whole world of text-based, flexible tools for managing data of various kinds. Tools like
Magit
and
Org-mode
offered (and still offer) unique ways to make sense of a codebase, track tasks, manage notes, automate and integrate with other systems, etc. This was "personal computing" at its purest; most modern GUI productivity apps felt like toys in comparison.
Emacs is a powerful tool, but it also demands a lot from its user. Eventually I got tired of dealing with the host of plugins and customizations that I needed to keep my system running the way I wanted. I'm at a point in my life where I would rather spend my spare time on hobbies, hanging out with family and friends, and otherwise not messing around with a patchwork of ELisp code snippets that I've cobbled together from various sources. I gradually stopped using Emacs in favor of more modern tools that are less flexible but also less of a hassle.
However, I often found myself missing some of the features that Emacs provided –
Org-Mode
in particular. Org-Mode is a tool for writing hierarchical text documents, and can serve as the foundation for an entirely text-based workflow for note-taking, agendas, and various forms of personal knowledge management. Once you get the hang of it, it's very intuitive. Some people manage their entire lives through Org-Mode and use it to have years of information at their fingertips.
Obsidian: An Org-Mode replacement?
​
I'm currently in the process of preparing for a new role on a new team at my job, and I have a lot of projects to get up to speed on. Enter
Obsidian
: a markdown-based text editor and note-taking app that has a lot of features useful for "personal knowledge management". Obsidian is proprietary software, but like Emacs it has an extensive system of
community-provided plugins
that support all kinds of different workflows (currently I'm using the
Tasks
and
Dataview
plugins, both of which let you dynamically aggregate different kinds of content from across documents in one place). Unlike Emacs, out-of-the-box usage of Obsidian is very straightforward (there's even a good Vim mode!), and there is a well-designed iOS client as well (the lack of an easy way to see tasks on a mobile device was one of the biggest limitations of Org-Mode in my experience).
Like Emacs, Obsidian can be used in a lot of different ways. If I'm going to be successful with this tool, I need to have a vision for how I want to use it. I did a little bit of research about frameworks for personal knowledge management and came across the
PARA
method. The basic idea behind PARA is that you file all your various notes or documents into 4 distinct folders:
Projects
(actionable, short-term),
Areas
(long-term responsibilities or recurring work),
Resources
(useful info to reference later), and
Archive
(anything from any other category that is no longer active). Uncategorized notes typically go into a dedicated inbox folder, and then get organized during a weekly review session. The system seems pretty simple, which I hope will help with being consistent over time. I'd rather have a simple system that I can consistently apply as opposed to a complicated one that I give up on after a few months. PARA is software-independent but it's easy to implement in Obsidian – a "vault" in Obsidian is just a collection of folders and files. My top-level vault structure looks like this:
00 Inbox/
01 Projects/
02 Areas/
03 Resources/
04 Archive/
Attachments/
Templates/
DASHBOARD.md
README.md
TODO.md
In addition to the PARA folders (which are numbered to keep them in the desired order) I have an Inbox, an "attachments" directory (Obsidian will put any attached files there automatically, keeping the rest of the structure uncluttered), a "templates" directory for re-usable content, and a small number of top-level files – a dashboard that pulls together items from various places (using the Dataview plugin), a master todo list (which pulls in tasks from all documents and organizes them, using the Tasks plugin), and a README file to remind me how things are structured. Everything else lives on one of these folders – typically the Inbox first, and then one of the PARA folders after review.
We'll see how well this works in practice, but this is my plan for now.
Why bother doing this?
​
I mentioned above that I stopped using Emacs because I no longer wished to spend the time or effort in fine-tuning and maintaining the custom workflows I was relying on. S

data.title: Gaussian integration is cool
data.author: beansbeansbeans
data.article_summary:
这篇文章简要介绍了高斯求积法中的切比雪夫-高斯求积法，用于计算定积分。切比雪夫-高斯求积法利用切比雪夫多项式的根作为节点，这些节点在区间边缘分布更密集，有助于减小多项式拟合时的震荡误差（如龙格现象）。与基本数值积分方法相比，高斯求积法在相同的节点数下可以处理更高阶的多项式，从而提高积分精度。

文章还讨论了如何将任意区间和函数形式转换为适合切比雪夫-高斯求积法的形式。通过适当的变换，可以将积分区间从$$a, b$$映射到$$[-1, 1]$$，并调整函数形式以适应求积公式。文章最后提到使用交互式笔记本工具（marimo notebook）来演示该方法，并提供了代码示例供读者尝试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕数值积分和相关数学概念的讨论

不同观点：
• Malipeddi认为文章对数值积分做了清晰易懂的介绍，并补充了嵌套求积法（如Gauss-Kronod与Clenshaw-Curtis/Fejér）的优点，即通过嵌套可以在提升精度时减少函数评估的总次数。
• algorithmsRcool提出了对博客安全性的担忧，声称其防病毒软件检测到可能的恶意脚本，特别是针对Windows和MSEDGE浏览器。
• tim-kt指出积分不能直接"表示"为权重和函数评估的总和，只能近似。他解释了通过固定节点、插值函数并积分多项式来获得求积和的原理，并强调高斯积分可以精确评估而非估计多项式的积分。
• actinium226对文章中的图表提出批评，认为图表的log刻度和截断原点的做法容易引起误解，建议直接比较两种方法的误差，而非其积分值。
• drmikeando分享了另一种类似的技术——tanh-sinh求积法，强调其在处理简单和复杂积分时的快速收敛特性。
• extrabajs询问图1的具体内容，质疑是否应展示积分的近似误差而非积分值本身。
• seanhunter最初以为文章是关于高斯积分（如e^(-x^2)从负无穷到正无穷的积分），并分享了其在数学中的美妙结果和个人学习经历。
• constantcrying强调了权重函数与正交多项式之间的紧密联系，指出不同权重函数对应不同类别的正交多项式，并提到Gauss-Hermite积分在整个实数范围内积分的特性。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及了数值积分的技术细节（如嵌套求积法、高斯积分的精确性）和应用问题（如图表展示、安全问题）。
- 争议的焦点包括图表展示的有效性和安全性问题，部分读者对图表设计提出质疑，而algorithmsRcool则担心网页安全性。
- 一些评论者分享了个人经验和相关技术，如tanh-sinh求积法和高斯积分的美妙数学结果，丰富了讨论的广度。

Elementary integration techniques work by approximating the function

with a polynomial. If we sample the function at n points, we can fit a polynomial of degree n-1, and integrate
that
to get the approximation. Basically this means that with n nodes, we can integrate polynomials with degree n-1. In contrast, Gaussian quadrature can estimate a polynomial of order 2n-1 with n nodes and another set of n weights. The weights are easily determined based on the specific technique, but now you need roughly half the number of function evaluations for an accurate integral approximation.
This is a great improvement in terms of numerical accuracy for the accuracy you get per function evaluation at a node. Gaussian quadrature does this by carefully selecting nodes - the nodes are given by the roots of an orthogonal polynomial function. These orthogonal polynomials act as a "basis", just like spline coefficients do for
spline fitting
(with the difference of global instead of local support). By the definition of orthogonality, these have an inner product (dot product in euclidean space) of zero with each other, and that simplifies the necessary calculations (

文章还讨论了如何将任意区间和函数形式转换为适合切比雪夫-高斯求积法的形式。通过适当的变换，可以将积分区间从$$a, b$$映射到$$[-1, 1]$$，并调整函数形式以适应求积公式。文章最后提到使用交互式笔记本工具（marimo notebook）来演示该方法，并提供了代码示例供读者尝试。
44215603.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕数值积分和相关数学概念的讨论

不同观点：
• Malipeddi认为文章对数值积分做了清晰易懂的介绍，并补充了嵌套求积法（如Gauss-Kronod与Clenshaw-Curtis/Fejér）的优点，即通过嵌套可以在提升精度时减少函数评估的总次数。
• algorithmsRcool提出了对博客安全性的担忧，声称其防病毒软件检测到可能的恶意脚本，特别是针对Windows和MSEDGE浏览器。
• tim-kt指出积分不能直接"表示"为权重和函数评估的总和，只能近似。他解释了通过固定节点、插值函数并积分多项式来获得求积和的原理，并强调高斯积分可以精确评估而非估计多项式的积分。
• actinium226对文章中的图表提出批评，认为图表的log刻度和截断原点的做法容易引起误解，建议直接比较两种方法的误差，而非其积分值。
• drmikeando分享了另一种类似的技术——tanh-sinh求积法，强调其在处理简单和复杂积分时的快速收敛特性。
• extrabajs询问图1的具体内容，质疑是否应展示积分的近似误差而非积分值本身。
• seanhunter最初以为文章是关于高斯积分（如e^(-x^2)从负无穷到正无穷的积分），并分享了其在数学中的美妙结果和个人学习经历。
• constantcrying强调了权重函数与正交多项式之间的紧密联系，指出不同权重函数对应不同类别的正交多项式，并提到Gauss-Hermite积分在整个实数范围内积分的特性。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及了数值积分的技术细节（如嵌套求积法、高斯积分的精确性）和应用问题（如图表展示、安全问题）。
- 争议的焦点包括图表展示的有效性和安全性问题，部分读者对图表设计提出质疑，而algorithmsRcool则担心网页安全性。
- 一些评论者分享了个人经验和相关技术，如tanh-sinh求积法和高斯积分的美妙数学结果，丰富了讨论的广度。

data.title: Focus and Context and LLMs
data.author: tarasglek
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大语言模型（LLM）在软件工程任务中的应用，特别是复杂编码任务的完成能力。作者指出，尽管LLM能够完成一些人类工程师难以应对的编码任务，但这种能力高度依赖于提供的上下文质量和严格的算法监督。文章批评了当前对“代理编码”工具的过度炒作，认为这些工具无法如宣传那样自动生成大量有用的软件。作者通过一个HTTP/2服务器项目的例子说明，LLM在编写代码时需要大量人工干预和精细的上下文管理，且生产JSON等格式时表现不佳。最终，作者强调，LLM的有效性取决于输入的上下文质量，目前仅在优秀工程师手中才能展现出真正 impressive 的结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）代理在编程开发中的实际应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• **tptacek的观点**：认为当前的LLM代理无法独立完成复杂的端到端开发任务，但可以显著加速开发过程。他分享了自己使用LLM的实际经验，指出LLM在辅助开发时并不需要过度优化提示技能，且在项目中可以通过人为调整和重组代码来提高效率。他强调，LLM的真正价值在于加速开发，而非完全替代人类开发者。

• **artembugara的观点**：关注帮助开发者向LLM提供正确上下文的工具。他提出了是否有创业公司专注于解决这一问题的疑问，暗示在实际开发中，向LLM输入适当的上下文是关键挑战之一。

• **summarity的观点**：分享了自己使用不同LLM工具的经验，指出某些工具在特定任务中表现出色，但在其他场景中表现不佳，尤其是涉及过多工具调用时模型容易混淆。他还提到，增加提示的上下文虽然有效，但回报率不高，目前尚未找到完美的解决方案。

• **mathgeek的观点**：批评了某些人对于LLM使用的自大态度，强调最好的教学应具备谦逊的态度。他认为， mediocre的开发者使用LLM得到平庸的结果，反映出人的因素在LLM应用中的重要性。

• **jmward01的观点**：提出需要一种具有无限上下文能力的LLM结构，认为当前的变压器模型虽然带来了进步，但其限制也日益显现，尤其是在处理大规模上下文时。

• **emorning3的观点**：从文章中得到的启示是“上下文就是一切”，并强调人类助理的必要性。他认为，尽管LLM在开发中起到重要作用，但人类辅助仍然是不可或缺的。

• **jumploops的观点**：推荐使用Claude Code，认为它是目前最有用的LLM工具之一，尽管难以解释其相对于其他工具的优势，但使用后能显著提升工作流效率。

• **__mharrison__的观点**：通过一个YouTube视频展示LLM在无需编码和少量提示的情况下构建复杂软件的可能性，认为LLM的潜力比许多人想象的要大。

• **briian的观点**：幽默地指出“vibe编码”中的自我认知差异，认为有些开发者高估了自己的随意态度。他同意需要更好的方式让LLM选择适当的上下文，但认为这不是一个难以解决的问题。

• **quantum_state的观点**：简洁地强调了上下文的重要性，暗示LLM的成功应用依赖于正确的输入和环境。

• **Workaccount2的观点**：指出LLM的编程能力不仅限于专业开发者使用，对于没有编程背景但需要计算机实现想法的人同样有用。他将LLM比作翻译软件，认为专业人士的批评忽视了这些工具对普通用户的实际价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于LLM在编程开发中的实际效用和局限性。一部分人认为LLM目前无法完成复杂的端到端任务，另一部分人则认为LLM已经显著加速了开发过程，并且在某些场景下表现出色。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于“上下文”的重要性，以及如何有效地向LLM提供适当的上下文，以提高其生成代码的准确性和效率。
• 最后，关于LLM是否主要为专业开发者设计，还是更适合没有编程背景的用户，存在不同的看法。这反映了LLM应用的广泛性和多样性。

44215726.article_content:
Table of Contents
LLMs Can Complete Hard Software Engineering Tasks.
Context is everything
I decided to write down some thoughts on
agentic coding
and why it’s a very hyped wrong turn.
Let me start with some background on my LLM experience. I adopted LLMs into my work in Aug 2020. I was sold when I saw that GPT-3 could generate usable SQL statements. Something that used to take 4-8 hours of RTFMing, now took 15min. I have since worked on
chatcraft.org
, various RAG frameworks, etc. I use
aider
heavily for work, frequently switch models, have been
struggling
with tool calling since before MCP as even an idea.
LLMs Can Complete Hard Software Engineering Tasks.
#
According to the Internet hive mind agentic coding tools can complete multiple implementations of complete software
(write code this way or FOMO). This
video
is a perfect example (if this were true we would be drowning in useful software). “ADHD software agents on meth” is how I would describe that approach to software engineering.
I would double down on influencer claims and say that LLM-enabled tools can complete software that a large fraction of currently employed engineers would fail at
However so far I’m only aware of 1 such end-to-end AI-written project:
HTTP/2 server
(
blog post
). This is the single most impressive code-gen project I’ve seen so far. I did not think this was possible yet.
Highlights from: Building a 100% LLM-written, standards-compliant HTTP 2.0 server from scratch with Gemini 2.5 Pro
A ridiculous amount of work went into feeding the LLM correct context
Author micromanaged LLM workflow to keep it progressing. LLMs would get stuck, author would split up tests, devised an algo for changing LLM context when LLM got stuck, devised a files-as-units-of-work strategy, etc
It would have been impossible to complete the test by relying on tool calling. This matches experience in aider
blog
. That’s ironic because tool calling is the unreliable foundation of current agentic hype. Another interesting thing is that producing JSON is very difficult for LLMs. Often ad-hoc formats that LLMs were not tuned for work better.
It took days just to stream all the API calls (Google is 2-4x faster than Anthropic) and weeks to get completed software
So yes, LLMs can write code, but instead of being free agents, they can only write software under intense algorithmic supervision by extremely stubborn software engineers. The irony is that under such tight controls even junior human software writers might succeed at this task.
Context is everything
#
The output produced by an LLM is only as good as the context fed into it (including the original question). This is a hard unsolved problem. Current agentic programming is similar (but much worse) to the
genetic algorithm
hype I remember for the 90s. Yes, brute-force works, but it’s often too expensive of a solution.
I think until we come up with a better way to curate context for LLMs, they will only be truly impressive in the hands of exceptional software engineers (
Kenton
and
Sean
are also incredible communicators).
In the meantime continue expecting mediocre results from mediocre people feeding LLMs mediocre context.

data.title: Binfmtc – binfmt_misc C scripting interface
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: **binfmtc** 是一个让 C 语言用于脚本编写的工具，解决了因编译步骤繁琐而选择解释型语言的问题。通过在 C 脚本中添加特定注释标记 `/*BINFMTC: ...*/` 并赋予执行权限，每次调用脚本时，系统会自动编译并执行程序。该工具利用 Linux 的 **binfmt_misc** 机制，在调用 C 脚本时自动调用编译器（如 gcc）生成临时二进制文件并运行。此外，还提供了一个类似 C shell 的 "real csh" 示例，用于日常系统管理任务。安装可通过添加特定源并使用 `apt-get` 完成，未来计划包括支持更多语言如 gcj、g77、mono 等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过不同方法实现C脚本或类似功能

不同观点：
• [rwmj] 提出了一种不使用 binfmt 的方式，通过条件编译和 shell 脚本结合，直接编译和运行 C 文件。他提到虽然可以用临时文件实现，但给出了一个无需 binfmt 的简单示例。
• [zx2c4] 提到了自己过去的一个类似项目，提供了一个链接，展示如何通过外部工具实现脚本化的 C 编译和执行。
• [monocasa] 提出了另一种方法，使用 tcc（tiny C compiler），其具有 shebang 兼容性，可以直接用于脚本。
• [radiospiel] 也分享了一个类似的方法，通过指向 C 编译器和运行器的 shebang 行实现。他质疑了通过 binfmt_misc 注册扩展的必要性。
• [kazinator] 强调这种方法完全可以在没有 Linux 特定的 binfmt-misc 黑科技的情况下实现，并提供了一个 Rosetta Code 上的多行 shebang 示例。
• [codr7] 分享了自己为书籍编写的一个简单黑科技，通过 C 程序内部实现类似的功能，并提供了 GitHub 链接。
• [rurban] 仅提到了一个年份 (2006)，可能暗示这种方法或类似想法早已存在。
• [elitepleb] 提到了一个类似的旧网页，展示了一种早期的实现方式。
• [enriquto] 惊讶地发现通过简单的包安装（binfmtc）就能在 Linux Mint 上实现类似的功能。
• [JSR_FDED] 表达了对 C 语言的喜爱，强调了 C 语言的简洁和直接，以及编程中的责任感。
• [Surac] 简短地表达了对这种方法的喜爱。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是是否需要使用 binfmt_misc 注册扩展。部分评论者质疑其必要性，认为有其他更简单和跨平台的方法。
• 各种方法的优劣被间接讨论，包括条件编译、外部工具、shebang 兼容性等不同实现方式。
• 一些评论者分享了个人项目或发现，提供了具体的示例和资源链接，丰富了讨论。

总体来看，讨论围绕着多种实现 C 脚本化编译和执行的方法展开，涉及到具体技术细节和个人偏好。

44216630.article_content:
binfmtc - binfmt_misc C scripting interface
Home
Back
Japanese
Introducing the binfmt_misc C scripting interface
"I love C".
"I enjoy writing in C".
"I don't feel well when I have passed a day without coding a line of C".
"My conversation with my wife simply doesn't flow without the C language".
"I want to write everything in C, even the everyday scripting,
but due to the steps required for writing make files and other things,
I tend to choose interpreted languages".
A good news for the C programmers suffering from these symptoms.
binfmtc is a hack to allow you to use the C language for cases where
script languages such as perl and shell were the languages of choice.
Also included is a "real csh" as an example, allowing you to use the
C language style for executing everyday sysadmin work.
Please experience the real C shell, which has a slightly different
tint to the original C shell we've been used to for more than 10 years.
Screenshots
Examples of execution in C, assembly, and C++.
The last entry is the one for real csh.
Usage
Simply add a magic keyword
/*BINFMTC:
compile-time options
and add execution permission to the C-script.
Every time you invoke the script, the compiler will compile and
execute the program for you.
How to install
For sid add the following line to /etc/apt/sources.list
and do
apt-get update; apt-get install binfmtc
.
deb http://www.netfort.gr.jp/~dancer/tmp/20050523 ./
Mechanics behind it
By registering magic through Linux binfmt_misc,
binfmtc-interpreter will be invoked every time a C script is invoked.
binfmtc-interpreter will parse the specified script file,
and will invoke gcc with the required options, and compile
to a temporary binary,
and invoke the binary.
Future plans
Do you actually find it, ... useful?

done

data.title: Show HN: Let’s Bend – Open-Source Harmonica Bending Trainer
data.author: egdels
data.article_summary: 《Let's Bend》是一款帮助初学者掌握口琴压音技巧的应用。压音技巧需要通过长期练习来掌握，可以让口琴发出常规吹奏无法达到的半音。该应用通过可视化音符，让学习过程更加简单有趣，适用于macOS、Debian、Windows以及Android等多种系统。Android版在Google Play、Amazon和F-Droid上免费提供，无广告。桌面版未在微软商店和苹果应用店发布，但可通过其他方式下载。应用还提供网页版、用户指南及源代码，并设有自愿捐赠功能，但整体保持免费。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于如何学习演奏和改进口琴技巧的工具、方法和资源的讨论。

不同观点：
• [kpgraham] 认为初学者应通过听觉学习口琴，强调听音和自然感受音符的变化，尤其是通过与音乐（如Little Walter的歌曲）一起演奏来提高技巧。他不太相信应用程序能有效帮助初学者掌握口琴的技巧。
• [p0w3n3d] 则支持使用软件工具来辅助学习，分享了自己在学习小提琴颤音时使用该软件获得良好效果的体验，认为这种工具能清晰显示音准问题，有助于练习。
• [j_m_b] 对软件工具表示赞赏，并提到自己曾开发过类似应用于吉他的工具，表达了对该技术在吉他学习上应用的兴趣。
• [Stratoscope] 提供了关于Melody Maker调音的详细建议，并分享了自己对不同调音方式在演奏流行/摇滚/乡村音乐中的优势的看法，尤其是对那些希望在口琴上演奏特定音阶的人提供了实用的建议。
• [SOLAR_FIELDS] 提供了初学者学习口琴音弯曲技巧的具体方法和步骤，强调了不同类型口琴和音区对学习弯曲技巧的影响。

补充讨论：
• [dhon_] 分享了一个关于音弯曲机制的解释视频，强调通过调整口腔共鸣腔的大小来实现音弯曲。
• [collingreen] 对项目表示赞赏，但对口琴技巧没有提供具体观点。
• [abdullahkhalids] 建议在工具中增加频率 vs 时间的对比图，以便视觉上跟踪音弯曲技巧的改进。
• [jimmar] 指出网站上缺乏对"bending"技巧的解释，建议添加相关说明或演示视频以帮助初学者理解。
• [LorenDB] 对软件中加入超吹目标表示赞赏，认为这是高级技巧且常被忽视。
• [philip-b] 推荐了一个名为"Bending Trainer"的应用程序，认为对学习音弯曲有帮助。
• [incognito124] 表示由于语言障碍，误解了讨论的主题，以为讨论的是手风琴。

争议焦点：
• 技术工具（应用程序）在学习口琴音弯曲技巧中的有效性。一些用户（如[kpgraham]）认为听觉和自然感受更为重要，而另一些用户（如[p0w3n3d]和[philip-b]）则支持使用应用程序来辅助学习。

44217757.article_content:
Let's Bend - Learn to play the harmonica and bend like a pro
For beginners,
bending
notes on a harmonica is a big hurdle. It requires a lot of time through regular practice. By bending, even the semitones can be sounded on the harmonica through special drawing and blowing techniques, which cannot be reached by regular playing of the channels. Beginners ask themselves, "Is that bending now or is the semitone exactly hit?"
The lean and performant
Lets' Bend
app makes it easy and fun for anyone to master the art of bending. By visualising the notes you play, you'll be bending like a pro in no time.
A short video about the functionality is published here:
Your browser does not support the video tag.
The original idea in developing the
Let's Bend
app was to create an application that is available on all common operating systems and whose application window scales well. It is not uncommon to have other applications open while practising or to want to use the programme on different devices. Last but not least, all keys and the most common special tunings of harmonicas should be supported.
As a result, there are now two versions of the app. A desktop version for the operating systems macOS, Debian and Windows, and an Android version for mobile devices.
The Android version is published free of charge and without advertising on
Google Play
,
Amazon
and
F-Droid
.
Since a publication on Microsoft Store and Apple App Store is associated with additional development costs that exceed the financial effort of a hobby development project, the desktop version was not published there. Instead,
here is an alternative download option for the desktop version.
As a preview, there is a
web version
available here.
For detailed instructions, check out our
User Guide
.
The source code of the applications is published
here.
If you would like to support the developer of
Let's Bend
by making a voluntary donation, there is a
Buy me a coffee
function in the desktop version. But even here,
Let's Bend
remains free of charge.
But enough talk now.
Let's Bend!

data.title: Administering immunotherapy in the morning seems to matter. Why?
data.author: abhishaike
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了免疫疗法在早晨施行的显著效果。研究发现，在下午3点前接受免疫疗法输注的患者，其癌症控制时间和生存期均显著延长。这一发现挑战了当前不考虑时间的标准护理方式。尽管有人怀疑研究可能存在问题，但该研究是随机临床试验，具有较高可信度。此外，先前多项研究也支持早晨进行免疫疗法效果更佳的结论，称为“免疫时间疗法”（immunochronotherapy）。对于不同类型的癌症，如肺癌、食道癌和黑色素瘤，早晨施治均显示出显著疗效。尽管部分研究为回顾性研究，但结合随机临床试验结果，证据表明早晨施治可能带来实质性的生存益处。这一现象可能与人体的昼夜节律有关。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：化疗和免疫治疗的时间安排与疗效及副作用之间的关系

不同观点：
• **化疗时间影响免疫系统抑制**：[raylad]分享其父亲接受氟达拉滨化疗时，通过研究发现癌细胞与免疫细胞的昼夜节律差异，将化疗安排在晚上，成功避免免疫系统过度抑制。医生虽对此印象深刻，但因缺乏临床研究且不便于操作，未改变治疗方案。
• **药物副作用的时间依赖性**：[unnamed76ri]提到通过改变服用叶酸的时间，缓解了化疗导致的口腔溃疡，暗示时间可能影响药物副作用。
• **免疫细胞耗竭与免疫治疗**：[EricPhy]用T细胞耗竭来比喻人类抑郁与倦怠，强调免疫治疗在重新激活耗竭T细胞方面的重要性。
• **对昼夜节律效应的怀疑**：[levocardia]对时间安排带来的显著效果表示怀疑，认为可能存在其他变量（如药物保存温度或随机化问题）导致结果，而非昼夜节律本身。
• **患者日常活动的影响**：[jmward01]提出患者日常活动（如上厕所）的时间可能影响治疗效果，强调需要考虑多种时间依赖因素。

补充讨论：
• **实际操作的可行性**：[aitchnyu]质疑医院是否应通过人工调节光线来改变患者昼夜节律，以适应最佳治疗时间，暗示实际操作中的困难。
• **医生决策依据**：[rendaw]对医生依据直觉而非研究做出决策表示怀疑，反映患者对医疗决策透明度的需求。
• **免疫治疗时间选择的科学依据**：[Noelia-]提到其同事医生选择早上进行免疫治疗，认为这背后有科学依据，呼应了时间对疗效的影响。
• **研究设计的变化**：[OrderlyTiamat]指出研究目标和设计多次改变，导致对统计结果的解释困难，质疑研究结论的可靠性。
• **潜在的治疗优化新层面**：[HexPhantom]认为时间生物学可能是治疗优化的新层面，暗示未来研究的重要性。
• **其他药物的时间效应**：[parsabg]提出免疫抑制剂用于自身免疫疾病是否也受时间影响的问题，拓展了讨论的范围。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **相关研究和资源**：[BDGC]提供UCSD的BioClock Studio资源以学习昼夜节律生物学概念，[egocodedinsol]提供研究摘要链接，为讨论提供了科学依据。
• **替代理论**：[pmlnr]提到身体子午线时钟理论，为时间生物学效应提供了另一种解释。

整体来看，评论主要围绕化疗和免疫治疗时间安排对疗效和副作用的影响，讨论了科学依据、实际操作可行性及研究可靠性等问题。

Edit on 08/06/2024: At least one person has pointed out that, at one point, giving hypertensives at night were
also
thought to matter,
a now disproven idea.
Someone also mentioned how many times the clinical trial information was altered during the study. I added in a section at the end to discuss this.
There’s a really interesting phenomenon in the immunotherapy field that has been going on for what seems to be several years now, but was raised to me — a non-oncologist —
via a viral Twitter thread
of some work at
ASCO25
:
Translating the jargon: amongst the patients who received their immunotherapy infusion before 3pm (as opposed to after 3pm), their
cancer stayed under control for longer
(11.3 months vs. 5.7 months) and
on median
lived longer
(at least
1
23.2 months versus 16.4 months). A near 2x~ improvement in the most important metrics doing something that is entirely risk-free and cost-free.
These two images shown in the comments
of the post also demonstrate genuine changes in levels of circulating T-cells between the two groups:
Important context: the current standard of care for immunotherapy is not designed with timing in mind.
You come in to get the injection when convenient for you or when there are free spots, there is no official recommendation to get it in the morning. But this study implies that we should potentially update our guidelines.
Weird, right? And if you have my relatively naive instincts, obviously wrong. Something
must
have been off in the study
. After all, wasn’t there that one paper about how time-a-lab-test-is-taken is more predictive of patient survival than the test results themselves?
The punchline? Sicker patients have strangely-timed emergency lab orders at 2AM, healthy patients have routine morning blood draws. Timing is hard to rely on!
But this paper was
not
a retrospective study of electronic health records, it was a randomized clinical trial, which is the gold standard. This means that we’ll be forced to immediately throw away our list of other obvious complaints against this paper. Yes, healthier patients may come in the morning more often, but randomization fixes that. Yes, patients with better support systems may come in the morning more often, but randomization fixes that. Yes, maybe morning nurses are fresher and more alert, but, again, randomization fixes that.
Okay. Well. Maybe there is something here. Caveats on this of course being a conference presentation without a corresponding, longer peer-reviewed paper, so we lack a lot of exact details on what exactly went on. Maybe the randomization used here is off for some reason, we’ll see once an official paper comes out.
But perhaps we should look beyond just this research.
As it turns out, there is an astonishing amount of pre-existing literature on the immense benefits in giving patients immunotherapy earlier in the day,
also known as ‘immunochronotherapy’
.
The exact time varies, but anytime before the evening seems to be good.
Here’s one study that found, again, a massive improvement when giving immunotherapy before 11:30AM for advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
And
again for esophageal cancer, before 1pm.
And again for
melanoma, before 4:30.
All of this culminated in a really incredible review paper that is really worth reading.
It walked through 18 retrospective studies covering 3,250 patients, each of which studied the impact of immunotherapy injection time on patient outcome. And, once you compile them all together, there is a very dependable story being told across multiple types of cancer.
TLDR: early-in-the-day immunotherapy administration consistently leads to massive improvements in survival time,
matching up quite well with the 2x results from the original Twitter post.
Keep in mind, these results have not only been shown for short-lived small molecules, but also long-lived proteins with half-lives on order of weeks that shouldn’t be affected by 24-hour cycles: pembrolizumab (Keytruda), nivolumab (Opdivo), and ipilimumab (Yervoy). Now, skepticism here would be justified given that these are all retrospective studies, and it’d be very easy for these to be confounded. But this evidence
combined
with the extremely similar results from the randomized clinical trial done I showed at the start of this essay should lead us towards at least suspecting that this is an honest-to-god free lunch.
What’s going on? Where is this coming from?
First, it’s worth reminding ourselves that the human body — and perhaps most complex life on Earth — exists on a schedule: the circa

• **免疫治疗时间选择的科学依据**：[Noelia-]提到其同事医生选择早上进行免疫治疗，认为这背后有科学依据，呼应了时间对疗效的影响。
• **研究设计的变化**：[OrderlyTiamat]指出研究目标和设计多次改变，导致对统计结果的解释困难，质疑研究结论的可靠性。
• **潜在的治疗优化新层面**：[HexPhantom]认为时间生物学可能是治疗优化的新层面，暗示未来研究的重要性。
• **其他药物的时间效应**：[parsabg]提出免疫抑制剂用于自身免疫疾病是否也受时间影响的问题，拓展了讨论的范围。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **相关研究和资源**：[BDGC]提供UCSD的BioClock Studio资源以学习昼夜节律生物学概念，[egocodedinsol]提供研究摘要链接，为讨论提供了科学依据。
• **替代理论**：[pmlnr]提到身体子午线时钟理论，为时间生物学效应提供了另一种解释。

整体来看，评论主要围绕化疗和免疫治疗时间安排对疗效和副作用的影响，讨论了科学依据、实际操作可行性及研究可靠性等问题。

data.title: Efficient mRNA delivery to resting T cells to reverse HIV latency
data.author: matthewmacleod
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种利用mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒（LNP）技术逆转HIV潜伏期的方法。研究人员开发了一种新型LNP配方（LNP X），能够在不引起细胞毒性或激活的情况下，将mRNA高效递送到难以转染的静息CD4+ T细胞中。通过封装编码HIV Tat蛋白的mRNA，LNP X增强了来自HIV感染者的CD4+ T细胞中HIV的转录。此外，LNP X还可以递送CRISPR激活机制，调节病毒和宿主基因的转录。这种方法为开发基于核酸的T细胞疗法提供了潜力，可能有助于清除HIV潜伏病毒库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MRNA技术在治疗潜伏病毒（如疱疹、水痘/带状疱疹）方面的潜在应用及公众教育的重要性

不同观点：
• [sroussey] 认为MRNA技术有可能用于治疗其他嵌入细胞的潜伏病毒，如疱疹和带状疱疹。这个评论提出了将MRNA技术扩展至其他病毒性疾病的设想，并关注其在医疗领域的广泛应用潜力。

• [Zigurd] 强调MRNA疗法的巨大潜力，但指出公众由于缺乏相关知识，容易被不科学的言论误导，甚至可能受到敌对国家势力的影响。Zigurd认为，加强公众教育和宣传是防止人们被误导的关键，并强调了这一问题的紧迫性和重要性。

补充讨论：
• [Zigurd] 进一步提出，公众因误导而受到的伤害不仅是个人层面的问题，还可能成为国家安全层面的问题，因为敌对国家可能会利用公众对MRNA技术的不了解来进行干预。这一论点将问题提升到了更广泛的社会和国际政治层面。

• 争议的焦点可能在于如何有效开展MRNA技术的公众教育，以及如何防止虚假信息和敌对势力的干预。这涉及科学传播、公共政策和国际关系等多方面的复杂问题。

Efficient mRNA delivery to resting T cells to reverse HIV latency
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
HIV infections
PCR-based techniques
Preclinical research
Retrovirus
Abstract
A major hurdle to curing HIV is the persistence of integrated proviruses in resting CD4
+
T cells that remain in a transcriptionally silent, latent state. One strategy to eradicate latent HIV is to activate viral transcription, followed by elimination of infected cells through virus-mediated cytotoxicity or immune-mediated clearance. We hypothesised that mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology would provide an opportunity to deliver mRNA encoding proteins able to reverse HIV latency in resting CD4
+
T cells. Here we develop an LNP formulation (LNP X) with unprecedented potency to deliver mRNA to hard-to-transfect resting CD4
+
T cells in the absence of cellular toxicity or activation. Encapsulating an mRNA encoding the HIV Tat protein, an activator of HIV transcription, LNP X enhances HIV transcription in ex vivo CD4
+
T cells from people living with HIV. LNP X further enables the delivery of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) activation machinery to modulate both viral and host gene transcription. These findings offer potential for the development of a range of nucleic acid-based T cell therapeutics.

Introduction
Recent advances in mRNA and lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology have allowed for the development of new vaccines and therapeutics, holding great promise for gene therapy. In 2018, patisiran (Onpattro) was approved as the first LNP-based therapeutic for the delivery of silencing (si)RNA for transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis
1
. The same platform has since been used to deliver mRNA to generate two of the most effective vaccines against COVID-19 (Comirnaty (Pfizer/BioNTech) and Spikevax (Moderna)). More recently, LNPs have been used to deliver mRNA for CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing in vivo, which was found to be safe in human clinical trials
2
. These advances have triggered enormous interest in the use of mRNA-LNPs as versatile therapeutics, including for infectious diseases such as HIV.
Whilst antiretroviral therapy (ART) effectively inhibits active HIV replication and reduces morbidity and mortality, it is not curative and treatment is life-long
3
. The major barrier to HIV cure is the persistence of latently infected, resting CD4
+
T cells harbouring replication-competent virus
4
,
5
,
6
, which can rebound following T cell activation and re-establish viremia in the absence of ART. One approach towards an HIV cure is to reactivate HIV transcription using latency-reversing agents (LRAs) while on ART, with the goal of subsequently inducing death of the infected cells and reduction of the HIV reservoir through viral cytopathic effects or immune-mediated clearance of the infected cell
7
,
8
. Traditionally, this has been achieved using small, hydrophobic compounds, that target different cellular pathways to activate transcription
9
,
10
. These first-generation LRAs, such as histone deacetylase inhibitors, can be administered systemically and passively cross the plasma membrane to exert their effect intracellularly. Several LRAs have demonstrated induction of HIV RNA in vitro, ex vivo and in clinical trials; yet, to date, no clinical trial of an LRA alone has shown a reduction in the size of the HIV reservoir
7
,
8
,
11
,
12
,
13
,
14
,
15
.
There are several hypotheses as to why LRAs alone have not been able to induce clearance of infected cells. First, most first-generation LRAs only increase the initiation of HIV transcription (as measured by unspliced HIV RNA), but fail to overcome subsequent blocks in transcription elongation, completion and splicing that persist in a resting CD4
+
T cell
10
. Second, first-generation LRAs are not HIV-specific, and therefore their potency to reactivate HIV is unavoidably coupled to off-target and adverse effects
8
,
16
,
17
. Indeed, certain LRAs have been shown to directly inhibit CD8
+
T cell and natural killer cell function in vitro, potentially hampering immune-mediated clearance of reactivated cells
18
,
19
. Therefore, there is a need for new LRAs that have greater potency, lower toxicity, and greater specificity for the HIV provirus.

data.title: Why Android can't use CDC Ethernet (2023)
data.author: goodburb
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了为何CDC Ethernet在Android设备上无法工作。原因在于Android的EthernetTracker服务只识别名为"ethX"的网络接口，而Linux的CDC Ethernet驱动创建的接口名为"usbX"。解决此问题的唯一方法是获取root权限，修改配置文件"config_ethernet_iface_regex"。

文章还介绍了如何通过ADB和USB调试来查找Android设备的内核配置，以确定设备支持的USB Ethernet适配器。由于手机厂商通常不公布支持列表，用户需通过内核配置或论坛经验来选择兼容的适配器。对于较新的Android设备，可以通过Google提供的Android Common Kernel及其分支来查找相关配置信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Android设备与CDC Ethernet适配器的兼容性问题及其引发的对内核接口命名和系统限制的讨论

不同观点：
• jordemort分享了自己在处理Android设备与CDC Ethernet适配器时的糟糕经历，并提到有人告诉他修改MAC地址的某一位可以使内核分配`ethX`名称而不是`usbX`名称，但他自己没有验证该方法，因为他已经换了工作且不再接触Android设备。
• progbits指出在2023年10月，Android的正则表达式已从`eth\\d`改为`*`，可能解决了此问题，并提到该更改可能已在Android 14中生效。
• franga2000通过查看LineageOS的提交历史，发现该问题经过了多次修复和回退，最终在最新Android版本中得到了解决，且Google可能参与了这些更改。
• 0xbadcafebee对EthernetTracker服务只识别`ethX`名称的接口表示强烈不满，认为这是过时的设计，提到Linux发行版早在2000年代就解决了类似问题，并指出现代内核可以通过udev等工具自动重命名接口。
• userbinator认为除了root手机以修改配置文件`config_ethernet_iface_regex`外，没有其他解决方法，强调了拥有root权限的重要性。
• rcxdude提到Android不能同时连接多个网络的问题，比如连接没有互联网的WiFi和手机网络时会出现问题，而Linux和Windows都可以做到这一点。

补充讨论：
• 404Escalation将此问题与OpenAI的对齐/升级系统问题进行了类比，认为都是由于未注意的正则表达式引发的问题。
• hypercube33和sollewitt讨论了USB Ethernet适配器的兼容性问题，提到大多数适配器使用Asix或Realtek的芯片组，并指出某些设备可能需要固件支持。
• kimixa补充了设备需要固件支持的问题，指出某些设备在Android UI中无法显示错误信息，只能通过dmesg查看。
• Zak提到Vanilla Android不支持ad-hoc WiFi网络的问题，并指出第三方ROM通常支持该功能。
• tripdout建议使用cs.android.com而不是下载整个100+ Gb的源码。
• MBCook提到iOS不支持CDC Ethernet适配器的问题，并询问iOS可能使用的其他标准。
• ahepp分享了自己在嵌入式系统上的经验，提到两个CDC Ethernet设备中一个显示为`ethX`，另一个显示为`usbX`，怀疑可能与不同的CDC子类有关。
• hansjorg质疑为什么文章中很晚才提到CDC的定义，认为应该更早解释该术语。

争议焦点：主要集中在Android系统对CDC Ethernet适配器的支持不完善以及接口命名问题，特别是对`ethX`和`usbX`名称的不同处理方式，以及是否有简单有效的解决方法。

44219405.article_content:
If you just want the answer to the question posed in the title, click the TLDR below and then move on with your day. Otherwise, buckle in, weâre going debugging; this post is mostly about my thought process and techniques I used to arrive at the answer rather than the answer itself.
TLDR:
Just tell me why CDC Ethernet doesn't work on Android
Android's EthernetTracker service only acknowledges interfaces that are named
ethX
; Linux's CDC Ethernet drivers create interfaces that are named
usbX
. There is no way to work around this, short of rooting the phone to change the value of
config_ethernet_iface_regex
.
Android contains support for USB ethernet adapters. Thereâs even menus for them!
This means that if you very carefully select a USB Ethernet adapter that you know has a chipset compatible with your Android device, you can plug it in and these settings will spring to life. How do you know what chipsets are compatible with your phone?
Hearsay!
Iâm not entirely kidding. If the company that you bought your phone from sells a USB ethernet adapter as an accessory to it, you have a pretty good chance of that one working. Otherwise, itâs hit-or-miss; phone manufacturers rarely, if ever, publish lists of supported Ethernet adapters. The best youâre going to get is finding a forum post from someone that has the same phone as you saying that they bought a particular adapter that worked, and hoping you can find the same thing to buy.
Or is it?
As you may know, if you dig deep beneath Androidâs Googly carapace, youâll find a Linux kernel. To build the Linux kernel, you must first configure it. This configuration determines what features and hardware the resulting kernel will support. Thus, the list of Ethernet adapters supported by your phone will more-or-less correspond to those selected in the kernel configuration for your phone, although itâs possible (but unlikely) that your phoneâs manufacturer doesnât ship all of the drivers that they build, or that they build additional third-party drivers separately.
So, in order to figure out what Ethernet adapters your phone supports, youâre going to want to find your phoneâs kernel configuration. How do we do that?
First, enable USB debugging and install ADB
If youâd like to follow along with this blog post, youâre going to need enable USB debugging and to install ADB (Android Debug Bridge) â this is a command-line tool that is used by developers to interact with Android devices. In this post, we will be using it to run shell commands on a phone.
Thereâs good documentation elsewhere on how to do these things so Iâm not going to waste time by rewriting it poorly. Instead, have some links:
First,
enable USB debugging
on your phone
Install ADB
on your computer
Run
adb shell
, which will give you a shell prompt on the phone.
Congratulations, you can now run commands on your phone. Type
exit
and press enter when youâre ready to exit the ADB shell.
Next, we need to switch things up so that ADB connects to the phone over the network, instead of via USB. We need to do this because weâre going to try plugging some network adapters into the phoneâs USB port, so we canât also use the port for debugging.
With your phone connected to your computer via USB:
Connect your phone to the same network as your computer via wifi
Figure out your phoneâs IP address - you can do this by digging around the Settings app, or you can try
adb shell ifconfig wlan0
With the phone still connected via USB, run
adb tcpip 5555
Disconnect the USB cable from the phone
Reconnect to the phone by running
adb connect YOUR_PHONE_IP:5555
(replacing YOUR_PHONE_IP with the IP address from the phone)
Try
adb shell
to make sure it still works
Once you have ADB working over the network, you can proceed with trying to figure out what version of the kernel your Android device is running.
If you have a newer phoneâ¦
These days, Google publishes an
Android Common Kernel
, which downstream phone manufacturers are required to derive their kernels from. The source to this kernel is hosted in a
Git repository at googlesource.com
.
If your phone shipped with Android 11 or later, you have something called a
GKI kernel
- in this case, Google builds the kernel and the phone manufacturer puts all of their model-specific secret sauce into kernel modules. In this case, you can find the configuration that Google is using by navigating to the appropriate branch of the kernel repository, and looking at the file
arch/$ARCH/configs/gki_defconfig
, where
$ARCH
is the processor architecture of your phone. For example, if your phone has a 64-bit ARM processor (and it almost certainly does) then you will find this configuration at
arch/arm64/configs/gki_defconfig
.
How do I find out for sure what kernel version and processor architecture my phone has?
Now that we have the ability to run shell commands on the phone, we can turn to good old
uname
to discover the kernel version and architecture thatâs

data.title: Cheap yet ultrapure titanium might enable widespread use in industry (2024)
data.author: westurner
data.article_summary: 研究人员在东京大学工业科学研究所开发了一种有效去除钛中氧气的方法，从而降低了生产高纯度钛的成本。传统上，由于从钛矿石中去除氧气的成本高昂，钛产品的应用受到限制。该团队使用基于稀土金属的创新技术，将钛的氧含量降低到0.02%。关键步骤是将熔融钛与钇金属或其化合物反应，生成低成本、无氧的钛合金，且钇可回收利用。尽管该方法产生的钛合金中含有最多1%的钇，可能影响其机械和化学性质，但该技术简化了生产流程，有助于钛在工业和消费品中的广泛应用。这项研究发表在《Nature Communications》上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钛金属的工业应用前景及其生产过程中的技术问题

不同观点：
• **钛难以广泛应用**：[digdugdirk] 认为，尽管钛在航空航天领域具有"酷因素"，但由于加工困难（如机床和刀具不适应、切屑易燃等问题），即使生产成本降低，钛也不太可能在工业中广泛使用。钛的高成本不仅来源于原材料，还包括其加工难度。
  
• **新方法仍存在问题**：[Aurornis] 指出，虽然新方法去除了钛中的氧，但却引入了钇，且含量高达1%。这使得该方法看似只是用一个问题替换了另一个问题，无法生产出“超纯钛”。

• **钇污染的影响及解决前景**：[phkahler]、[neutrinobro] 和 [LasEspuelas] 等人关注钇污染对钛合金性能的影响，并讨论了解决该问题的可能性和迫切性。一些人质疑钇问题对工业应用的实际影响程度，以及未来是否容易解决。

• **历史视角与加工难度**：[duffpkg] 引用了《Skunk Works: A Personal Memoir of My Years at Lockheed》一书，指出钛加工困难的历史背景，并认为即便钛成本降低，控制成本仍然非常困难。

• **能源与成本的关系**：[westurner] 强调钛的高生产成本源于其制备过程中的高能耗，并提供了一篇相关研究文章的链接，指出解决这一问题对于工业和消费品开发的重要性。

• **其他合金的比较与个人体验**：[zafka] 提到镍钛诺合金（Nitinol）的发展历史，暗示类似的高性能材料也有过逐步普及的过程。而[eth0up] 则分享了个人使用钛制品的积极体验，强调了钛的实用性和耐用性。

• **对消费品应用的批评**：[exabrial] 批评了在消费品（如手机、手表）中使用钛的做法，认为不锈钢更适合，并表示对过度追求“钛”这一材料的时尚趋势感到厌倦。

• **专利与技术前景**：[foota] 提到该技术已经申请了专利，暗示该研究可能具有商业化潜力。

• **能源成本与技术发展**：[jjcm] 认为随着能源成本的下降（如太阳能和核聚变技术的进步），钛的生产成本可能随之下降，并质疑当前的中间步骤是否必要。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中存在对钛合金性能（如钇污染）的争议，以及对未来技术发展能否解决这些问题的不同看法。
• 有人提到钛在消费品中的应用可能更多是出于市场营销考虑，而非实际性能需求。
• 技术专利的提及指向了该研究可能带来的商业价值和应用前景。

Cheap yet ultrapure titanium metal might enable widespread use in industry
by
University of Tokyo
Researchers from the Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo, have efficiently removed oxygen from high-oxygen-concentration titanium, which might help reduce the production cost of an otherwise versatile metal. Credit: Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo
×
close
Researchers from the Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo, have efficiently removed oxygen from high-oxygen-concentration titanium, which might help reduce the production cost of an otherwise versatile metal. Credit: Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo
Titanium is the ninth most abundant element in the Earth's crust, yet products based on pure titanium are uncommon because it's expensive to remove the oxygen from titanium ore. Reducing costs would encourage manufacturers to take advantage of the highly useful properties of titanium in their products.
Now, in a study
published
in
Nature Communications
, researchers from the Institute of Industrial Science, The University of Tokyo, have developed a procedure that reduces the cost of producing titanium that's almost entirely free of
oxygen
. This oxygen removal protocol might benefit
technological development
and environmental sustainability.
Titanium is an incredibly versatile material because not only does it typically resist chemical damage, it's strong yet light. For example, its light weight compared with other metals is why the base frame of modern iPhones consists of titanium alloy, despite the increased cost.
Unfortunately, producing ultrapure titanium is significantly more expensive than manufacturing steel (an iron alloy) and aluminum, owing to the substantial use of energy and resources in preparing high-purity titanium. Developing a cheap, easy way to prepare it—and facilitate product development for industry and common consumers—is the problem the researchers aimed to address.
"Industry mass-produces iron and aluminum
metal
—but not titanium metal, because of the expense of removing the oxygen from the ore," explains Toru H. Okabe, lead author of the study. "We use an innovative technology based on
rare-earth metals
that removes oxygen from titanium to 0.02% on a per-mass basis."
Get free science updates with Science X Daily and Weekly Newsletters —
subscribe now
to customize your preferences!
A critical step in the researchers' protocol is reacting molten titanium with yttrium metal and yttrium trifluoride or a similar substance. The end result is a low-cost, solid, de-oxygenated titanium alloy. The reacted yttrium can be recycled for further use. A highlight of the researchers' work is that even titanium scrap that contains large amounts of oxygen can be processed in this manner.
"We're excited by the versatility of our protocol," says Toru H. Okabe. "The lack of intermediate compounds and straightforward procedures will facilitate adoption in industry."
This work is an important step forward in making more efficient use of high-purity titanium than at present. A limitation of this work is that the resulting de-oxygenated titanium contains yttrium, up to 1% by mass; yttrium can influence the mechanical and chemical properties of
titanium
alloy. After solving the yttrium contamination problem, applications to industrial manufacturing will be straightforward.
More information:
Toru H. Okabe et al, Direct production of low-oxygen-concentration titanium from molten titanium,
Nature Communications
(2024).
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-024-49085-4

data.title: Panjandrum: The ‘giant firework’ built to break Hitler's Atlantic Wall
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了二战期间盟军为突破德军“大西洋壁垒”而设计的一种名为“Panjandrum”的奇特武器。大西洋壁垒是德军在占领欧洲后建造的长达5000公里的防御工事，旨在抵御盟军的海上入侵。1942年迪耶普突击战的失败显示出直接攻击港口非常困难。为了减少士兵伤亡，英国工程师尼维尔·舒特·挪威（Nevil Shute Norway）带领团队设计了Panjandrum，一种可携带一吨炸药的“巨型烟花”，计划从海上发射，突破混凝土防御墙。然而，该武器的设计和测试过程中遇到许多问题，最终未被实际使用。这一计划展现了战争中盟军在面对防御工事时的创新思维与挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国二战期间的全面动员、技术创新以及具体军事项目的有效性和历史细节。

不同观点：
• [kjellsbells] 强调二战期间英国全民动员的程度，并指出英国文化中对古怪但聪明的天才的推崇，提到了电视节目《The Great Egg Race》作为例子。
• [j00pY] 分享了居住地附近的混凝土墙测试遗迹的历史，这些墙被用来研究最佳的爆破方法，并提供了相关链接以获取更多信息。
• [helsinkiandrew] 推荐了1970年代BBC的纪录片系列《The Secret War》，其中涵盖了各种技术项目，并提供了具体剧集链接，强调了采访参与者的价值。
• [thenthenthen] 对‘Panjandrum’的命名来源表示好奇，并质疑为何未采用已有的无线电导航技术，是否因战争中的干扰问题导致其不可靠。
• [anentropic] 认为‘Panjandrum’设计上的缺陷明显，如火箭推力不平衡导致的转向问题和高重心带来的不稳定性，怀疑其设计可能是有意作为误导。
• [hermitcrab] 提到美国也有自己的疯狂武器，如“蝙蝠炸弹”，将讨论扩展到其他国家在二战中的技术创新。
• [KineticLensman] 提到电视剧《Dad's Army》中再现了‘Panjandrum’，强调了其设计上的荒谬性，并提供了相关链接。
• [sevensor] 推荐阅读Nevil Shute的作品，特别是《Round the Bend》，将讨论引向文学领域。
• [daverol] 更欣赏‘Operation Pluto’中的‘Conundrum’设计，强调其在后勤方面的卓越表现，而非爆炸效果，并提供了相关链接。
• [hoseja] 认为‘Panjandrum’是一个愚蠢的装置，并指出诺曼底海滩的防御工事主要是战壕和沙袋，而非《Saving Private Ryan》中展现的碉堡，并提供了具体历史事件链接。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于‘Panjandrum’设计的实际有效性和目的，部分评论者认为其设计缺陷明显，可能是故意作为误导工具。
- 讨论中提到了多个具体历史事件和项目链接，如‘Panjandrum’、‘Operation Pluto’、‘Bat bomb’等，丰富了技术创新的背景。
- 对二战期间不同国家的技术研发和应用进行了对比和延展，展示了战争中各方为取得优势而进行的各种尝试。

Panjandrum: The 'giant firework' built to break Hitler's Atlantic Wall
4 days ago
Share
Save
Stephen Dowling
Share
Save
Imperial War Museums
To make D-Day a success, the Allies thought they might have to break through formidable German defences. One unconventional idea was a "giant firework" that would deliver a one-tonne bomb: the Panjandrum.
After conquering much of Western Europe in the first few years of World War II, Nazi Germany then diverted a huge effort into protecting what it had invaded.
Once the United States entered the war on the side of the Allies in late 1941, the threat of invasion from the sea went from a distinct possibility to certainty.
To prevent it, hundreds of thousands of forced labourers – some of them Russian prisoners captured on the Eastern Front – were set to work. They built walls, tank traps and reinforced-concrete emplacements. The fortifications stretched around 5,000km (3,105 miles) from France's border with Spain all the way to the northern tip of Norway.
Adolf Hitler called it the "
Atlantic Wall
", and there are still many traces of it, littering beaches from the Bay of Biscay to the sub-Arctic fjords.
Allied military planners had many challenges to wrestle with during their long preparations for the liberation of Europe. Seizing a port made the most sense – it would be easier to get vital supplies to the troops on the beachhead by unloading ships more speedily on the docks. But the ports on the English Channel coast had been heavily fortified by German defenders.
Alamy
The 1942 raid on Dieppe showed that the German defences around Channel ports were too strong for beach landings (Credit: Alamy)
A bold plan to temporarily take over one of these ports – Dieppe, in France –
in August 1942
showed how difficult a port would be to capture. Thousands of mostly Canadian troops were killed or captured in a botched attempt to push through defences; supporting tanks became bogged down on loose shingle sand and the built-up surroundings gave the defenders plenty of cover from which to fire on the invading forces.
Dieppe, it turned out, had the wrong kind of beach. The French coast had plenty of beaches firm enough to support tanks and other vehicles coming ashore, but these beaches would be overlooked by the Atlantic Wall defences the Germans were quickly building. How could they be breached, with the minimum loss to Allied soldiers? An eccentric plan was born…
The brilliant engineer behind a bizarre idea
Nevil Shute Norway was an accomplished aeronautical engineer who had worked on one of Britain's most high-profile airship designs. The
R100 airship
had been designed by engineer
Barnes Wallis
– who would later invent the
bouncing bomb
of Dambusters fame – for engineering firm Vickers, with funding from the government. Norway later took over as chief engineer when Wallis left to work on other projects.
The R100, intended for long-distance voyages across the British Empire, carried out successful
publicity tours
as far afield as Canada. It was developed alongside a similar airship designed and built by the UK's Air Ministry, called R101; this design was fatally flawed, and crashed with the loss of 48 lives in northern France while on its maiden flight.
News of the crash flashed around the world, killing Britain's emerging airship industry for good, and Norway drifted into more conventional aircraft designs, including the highly successful
Oxford trainer
designed by his own aircraft company, Airspeed.
The Directorate of Miscellaneous Weapon Development was known informally as the 'wheezers and dodgers'
When war broke out, Norway joined the Royal Navy Volunteer Reserve, initially serving on naval ships. But his flair for engineering took him in a different direction: into the navy's secret department for experimental weapons.
The
Directorate of Miscellaneous Weapon Development
was known informally as the "wheezers and dodgers". They drew bookish, lab-bound talent from the UK's universities and research institutes and challenged them to come up with new weapons that could be used in the war. No idea, however outlandish, was discouraged.
One of the weapons the British armed forces needed was something that could be deployed from a ship and was powerful enough to breach the strong concrete sea wall now in place across much of Europe. From there, Allied forces could hopefully capture the ports needed to sustain a sea invasion from behind, where they would be less well-defended.
Alamy
As the war progressed, German occupiers poured enormous resources into the Atlantic Wall to prevent a seaborne invasion (Credit: Alamy)
Norway and team did the calculations and arrived at a minimum explosive weight to break through the concrete defences: a tonne of high explosives. Placed against the wall, this should be enough to blow a tank-sized hole that will allow invading troops and vehicles to pour through. But to drive it up across a well-defended beach was likely to be too hazardous.

《Compiler Explorer在2025年的工作原理》介绍了这一工具如何处理每年9200万次的编译请求。文章详细描述了从用户在Monaco编辑器中输入代码，到代码通过CloudFront和负载均衡器发送至服务器，并进入编译队列的过程。服务器使用nsjail工具创建一个隔离环境运行编译器，生成输出结果并过滤无关信息，最终以JSON格式返回浏览器渲染。

为了应对高负载，系统会自动扩展各集群的实例数量。安全性方面，通过nsjail实现严格的进程隔离，防止用户执行任意代码。文章还提到管理近4TB的编译器版本通过大量Python和shell脚本实现，且坚持不淘汰旧版本以避免链接失效。这种做法不仅保证了稳定性，还为用户提供了长久的编译环境。
